observations.text: Re-review of the design delta only, at ff737aa. Re-read: git diff 53ffb7f ff737aa --stat shows the delta is docs-only (architecture.md and its html, handoff.json, plus the published review record); architecture.md:241 now fixes the control contract, "aria-controls naming the rail primary navigation, and an aria-label that names the SUBJECT as the nav, the current state and what the next press does: Left nav: expanded. Collapse the left nav. and Left nav: collapsed. Expand the left nav.", states the wording is fixed rather than left to the crafter, and states the id is SERVER-RENDERED, exactly one id attribute on the existing nav.sidebar__nav in partials/sidebar.html, keeping the asset to its two DOM effects; architecture.md:156, :367 and :509 carry the same one-id edit through the read-only target, the reuse row and the impact row, each saying no element, class, link or form is added, renamed or removed and that an id is inert with scripting off. Both findings are answered without touching a reviewed byte: git diff --stat 53ffb7f HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance is empty, so the oracle and its supports are identical to the bytes accepted in the first round, and the working tree carried no modification to them at re-review time. Judged against the delta: the two fixed labels each contain the token the oracle checks, differ from each other so the changed-by-the-press arm still bites, and leave aria-expanded as the exact state channel; getElementById on a server-rendered id resolves to the same nav element the probe compares against, so the stimulus to observation to falsifier chain for P4 is now complete in the design as well as in the oracle. No rerun was required or performed and no earlier run is restamped: the oracle bytes, the supports and the runtime are unchanged, so the RED evidence of the first round stands as recorded there (reused 32-case run plus the new degraded-lane execution at 53ffb7f, exit 101, 1 passed and 2 semantic RED). Every other judgment of the first round is retained unexamined, as the delta affects no other obligation. typesafe: unavailable still holds for this round; no judgment service call was attempted again.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED, re-review of the design delta only at ff737aa. Both first-round findings are resolved by authority and are removed: partials/sidebar.html is now a declared Extend target for exactly one id on the existing nav.sidebar__nav, so the aria-controls the oracle resolves through getElementById has a server-rendered supplier and the collapse asset keeps its two declared DOM effects; and the design now fixes the toggle label to "Left nav: expanded. Collapse the left nav." and "Left nav: collapsed. Expand the left nav.", which names the subject, differs between the two states and satisfies the oracle subject check, so that check is authority-backed rather than over-restrictive. No reviewed byte changed: git diff --stat 53ffb7f HEAD -- crates/foundry-acceptance is empty, so the oracle and its supports are the bytes accepted in the first round, the production edits a crafter is making lie outside those paths, and no rerun was required or performed. The RED evidence of the first round stands as recorded, the reused 32-case run with 0 parsing and 0 hook errors plus the new degraded-lane execution at 53ffb7f with exit 101, one already-satisfied P5 pass and two semantic RED. Every judgment outside this delta is retained unexamined, including the authority-backed limits on first-frame pixels, the unreachable storage-refused press on a signed-in screen and the JS-runner deviation for the broad half of L5. typesafe: unavailable still holds, so this round is reviewer_reason from local evidence. No finding remains; craft proceeds. Completion obligations unchanged: implementation GREEN for all 32 cases, and close evidence that names the lane that actually ran, because a gate without Docker observes none of these scenarios.
